## AI Agents for Beginners - 9. Metacognition in AI Agents
This post summarizes Lesson 09 from Microsoft's **AI Agents for Beginners** course.  
> Source: [microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners - 09-metacognition](https://github.com/microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners/tree/main/09-metacognition)

---

### What is Metacognition?

<mark>Metacognition</mark> is "thinking about thinking."  
In AI agents, metacognition refers to the ability of an agent to recognize its own internal processes and monitor, regulate, and adapt its behavior.

Key challenges addressed by metacognition:

| Challenge | Description |
|---|---|
| **Transparency** | The agent must be able to explain its reasoning and decisions |
| **Reasoning** | Enhances the ability to synthesize information and make sound decisions |
| **Adaptation** | Adapts to new environments and changing conditions |
| **Perception** | Improves accuracy in perceiving and interpreting environmental data |

Why metacognition is important in agent design:

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Importance of Metacognition"
}
---
flowchart LR
    MC["Metacognition\nRecognizing Own Thought Process"]
    MC --> SR["Self-Reflection\nEvaluating Performance & Identifying Improvement Areas"]
    MC --> AD["Adaptability\nAdjusting Strategy Based on Past Experience"]
    MC --> EC["Error Correction\nAutonomous Error Detection & Correction"]
    MC --> RM["Resource Management\nOptimizing Time & Compute Resources"]
```

**Core examples of metacognition**:
- "I prioritized cheap flights... but I might have missed direct flights. Let me check again."
- "Whenever the user said 'it's too complicated,' the issue was that I recommended items based on popularity."

The agent components—**Persona, Tools, and Skills**—combine to form an "expertise unit" that executes specific tasks, and metacognition enables this unit to improve on its own.

---

### Planning in Agents

<mark>Planning</mark> is a core element of AI agent behavior that designs steps to achieve a goal while taking into account the current state, resources, and obstacles.

9-step planning process of a travel agent:

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Travel Agent Planning Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    P1["1. Gather Preferences\nCollect dates, budget, interests"]
    --> P2["2. Retrieve Information\nSearch flights, hotels, attractions"]
    --> P3["3. Generate Recommendations\nCreate personalized itinerary"]
    --> P4["4. Present to User\nShare itinerary"]
    --> P5["5. Collect Feedback\nGather user feedback"]
    --> P6["6. Adjust Based on Feedback\nUpdate itinerary"]
    --> P7["7. Final Confirmation\nFinal review"]
    --> P8["8. Book & Confirm\nProceed with booking"]
    --> P9["9. Ongoing Support\nSupport during trip"]
```

Travel Agent implementation applying metacognition:

```python
{
    "title": "travel_agent_metacognition.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class Travel_Agent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.user_preferences = {}
        self.experience_data = []  # # [!code highlight]

    def gather_preferences(self, preferences):
        self.user_preferences = preferences

    def retrieve_information(self):
        flights = search_flights(self.user_preferences)
        hotels = search_hotels(self.user_preferences)
        attractions = search_attractions(self.user_preferences)
        return flights, hotels, attractions

    def generate_recommendations(self):
        flights, hotels, attractions = self.retrieve_information()
        return create_itinerary(flights, hotels, attractions)

    def adjust_based_on_feedback(self, feedback): # [!code highlight]
        self.experience_data.append(feedback) # [!code highlight]
        self.user_preferences = adjust_preferences(self.user_preferences, feedback) # [!code highlight]
        return self.generate_recommendations()

travel_agent = Travel_Agent()
preferences = {
    "destination": "Paris",
    "dates": "2025-04-01 to 2025-04-10",
    "budget": "moderate",
    "interests": ["museums", "cuisine"],
}
travel_agent.gather_preferences(preferences)
itinerary = travel_agent.generate_recommendations()

feedback = {"liked": ["Louvre Museum"], "disliked": ["Eiffel Tower (too crowded)"]}
new_itinerary = travel_agent.adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback) # [!code word:adjust_based_on_feedback]
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Metacognition Loop"
}
---
flowchart TD
    G["gather_preferences()\nInitialize preferences"]
    --> R["generate_recommendations()\nSearch flights/hotels/attractions + Generate itinerary"]
    --> U["Present itinerary to user"]
    --> FB["User Feedback\n{liked, disliked}"]
    FB --> Adj["adjust_based_on_feedback()\nAccumulate experience_data\nReadjust preferences"]
    Adj -->|"Updated Preferences"| R
```

Accumulating feedback in `experience_data`, readjusting preferences with `adjust_based_on_feedback`, and generating a new itinerary forms the core of the <mark>metacognition loop</mark>.

```adcard
```

---

### Corrective RAG System

Comparing two information access strategies:

| | **Corrective RAG** | **Pre-emptive Context Load** |
|---|---|---|
| **Approach** | Retrieve information from external sources at query time | Pre-load relevant context prior to processing |
| **Updates** | Real-time information | Pre-loaded information |
| **Speed** | Incurs retrieval latency | Immediate response |
| **Accuracy** | Feedback-based error correction | Fixed context |
| **Best For** | Dynamic data, when error correction is needed | Known domain, when fast responses are required |

```mermaid
{
    "title": "RAG Tool Calling vs Pre-Emptive Context Load"
}
---
%%{init: {'look': 'handDrawn'}}%%
flowchart TD
    subgraph RAG["RAG Tool Calling"]
        direction TD
        LLM1["LLM"]
        LLM1 --> T1["Tool"]
        LLM1 --> T2["Tool"]
        LLM1 --> T3["Tool"]
        T1 & T2 & T3 --> R1["Response"]
    end

    subgraph PCL["Pre-Emptive Context Load"]
        direction TD
        LLM2["LLM"]
        LLM2 --> CTX["Context\n(Provided before query processing)"]
        CTX --> R2["Response"]
    end
```

#### Corrective RAG Approach

<mark>Corrective RAG</mark> corrects errors and improves accuracy through three components:

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| **Prompting Technique** | Crafting specific prompts that guide the agent to retrieve relevant information |
| **Tool** | Implementing algorithms and mechanisms to evaluate the relevance of retrieved information and generate accurate responses |
| **Evaluation** | Continuously evaluating agent performance and iterating on adjustments to improve accuracy and efficiency |
```adcard
```
#### Step-by-Step Implementation of Corrective RAG

Five steps to applying Corrective RAG to a Travel Agent:

**Step 1 — Gather User Input**

Collect travel preferences such as destination, dates, budget, and interests.

```python
{
    "title": "step1_preferences.py"
}
---
preferences = {
    "destination": "Paris",
    "dates": "2025-04-01 to 2025-04-10",
    "budget": "moderate",
    "interests": ["museums", "cuisine"],
}
```

**Step 2 — Retrieve Information and Generate Initial Recommendations**

Search for flights, hotels, and attractions based on the collected preferences and generate an initial itinerary.

```python
{
    "title": "step2_retrieve.py"
}
---
flights     = search_flights(preferences)
hotels      = search_hotels(preferences)
attractions = search_attractions(preferences)

itinerary = create_itinerary(flights, hotels, attractions)
print("Suggested Itinerary:", itinerary)
```

**Step 3 — Collect User Feedback**

Collect positive and negative user feedback on the initial recommendations.

```python
{
    "title": "step3_feedback.py"
}
---
feedback = {
    "liked": ["Louvre Museum"],
    "disliked": ["Eiffel Tower (too crowded)"], # [!code highlight]
}
```

**Step 4 — Apply Corrective RAG**

- <mark>Prompting Technique</mark>: Formulate a new search query reflecting the feedback

```python
{
    "title": "step4_prompting.py"
}
---
if "disliked" in feedback: # [!code highlight]
    preferences["avoid"] = feedback["disliked"] # [!code highlight]
```

- <mark>Tool</mark>: Re-search with updated preferences and generate a new itinerary

```python
{
    "title": "step4_tool.py"
}
---
new_attractions = search_attractions(preferences)  # Reflecting avoid
new_itinerary   = create_itinerary(flights, hotels, new_attractions)
print("Updated Itinerary:", new_itinerary)
```

- <mark>Evaluation</mark>: Continuous evaluation function reflecting feedback into preferences

```python
{
    "title": "step4_evaluation.py"
}
---
def adjust_preferences(preferences, feedback): # [!code word:adjust_preferences]
    if "liked" in feedback: # [!code highlight]
        preferences["favorites"] = feedback["liked"] # [!code highlight]
    if "disliked" in feedback: # [!code highlight]
        preferences["avoid"] = feedback["disliked"] # [!code highlight]
    return preferences

preferences = adjust_preferences(preferences, feedback)
```

**Step 5 — Putting It Together: Corrective RAG Travel Agent**

This final example integrates the above steps into a single class. `adjust_based_on_feedback` handles feedback accumulation → preference update → new itinerary generation all in one go.

```python
{
    "title": "corrective_rag_travel_agent.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class Travel_Agent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.user_preferences = {}
        self.experience_data = []

    def gather_preferences(self, preferences):
        self.user_preferences = preferences

    def retrieve_information(self):
        flights     = search_flights(self.user_preferences)
        hotels      = search_hotels(self.user_preferences)
        attractions = search_attractions(self.user_preferences)
        return flights, hotels, attractions

    def generate_recommendations(self):
        flights, hotels, attractions = self.retrieve_information()
        return create_itinerary(flights, hotels, attractions)

    def adjust_based_on_feedback(self, feedback): # [!code highlight]
        self.experience_data.append(feedback) # [!code highlight]
        self.user_preferences = adjust_preferences(self.user_preferences, feedback) # [!code highlight]
        return self.generate_recommendations() # [!code highlight]

travel_agent = Travel_Agent()
preferences = {
    "destination": "Paris",
    "dates": "2025-04-01 to 2025-04-10",
    "budget": "moderate",
    "interests": ["museums", "cuisine"],
}
travel_agent.gather_preferences(preferences)
itinerary = travel_agent.generate_recommendations()
print("Suggested Itinerary:", itinerary)

feedback = {"liked": ["Louvre Museum"], "disliked": ["Eiffel Tower (too crowded)"]}
new_itinerary = travel_agent.adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback) # [!code word:adjust_based_on_feedback]
print("Updated Itinerary:", new_itinerary)
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Corrective RAG Travel Agent Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    GP["gather_preferences()\nStore destination, budget, interests"]
    --> GR["generate_recommendations()\nCall retrieve_information()"]
    GR --> RT["search_flights + hotels + attractions"]
    RT --> CI["create_itinerary()"]
    CI --> SU["Present itinerary to user"]
    SU --> FB["User Feedback\n{liked, disliked}"]
    FB --> AF["adjust_based_on_feedback()\nexperience_data.append(feedback)\nadjust_preferences() → Update preferences"]
    AF -->|"Updated user_preferences"| GR
```

#### Corrective RAG Flow

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Corrective RAG Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    User["User Input\nDestination, budget, interests"]
    --> Retrieve["Retrieve Information\nFlights, hotels, attractions"]
    --> Gen["Generate Initial Itinerary"]
    --> Feedback["Collect User Feedback"]
    Feedback --> Adjust{Analyze Feedback}
    Adjust -->|"disliked items"| NewQuery["Rewrite Query\nAdd preferences['avoid']"]
    NewQuery --> Retrieve
    Adjust -->|"Satisfied"| Done["Finalize Itinerary"]
```

#### Pre-emptive Context Load

Pre-loads known domain knowledge into memory before processing to respond immediately without external retrieval:

```python
{
    "title": "preemptive_context.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class TravelAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.context = { # [!code highlight]
            "Paris": {
                "country": "France", "currency": "Euro",
                "language": "French",
                "attractions": ["Eiffel Tower", "Louvre Museum"],
            },
            "Tokyo": {
                "country": "Japan", "currency": "Yen",
                "language": "Japanese",
                "attractions": ["Tokyo Tower", "Shibuya Crossing"],
            },
        }

    def get_destination_info(self, destination): # [!code word:get_destination_info]
        info = self.context.get(destination)
        if info:
            return (
                f"{destination}:\nCountry: {info['country']}\n"
                f"Currency: {info['currency']}\n"
                f"Attractions: {', '.join(info['attractions'])}"
            )
        return f"Sorry, we don't have information on {destination}."

travel_agent = TravelAgent()
print(travel_agent.get_destination_info("Paris"))
print(travel_agent.get_destination_info("Tokyo"))
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Pre-emptive Context Load Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    Init["__init__()\nPre-load self.context\n{Paris, Tokyo, NY, Sydney}"]
    --> Query["User destination query"]
    --> Get["get_destination_info(destination)\nself.context.get(destination)"]
    Get --> Check{Context exists?}
    Check -->|"Yes"| Hit["country, currency, language, attractions\nReturn immediately (no external retrieval)"]
    Check -->|"No"| Miss["Return 'No information available'"]
```

```adcard
```

### Bootstrapping a Plan with a Goal Before Iterating

An approach where a goal is defined upfront, followed by iterative refinement of the plan.  
Initial planning is established with <mark>bootstrap_plan</mark>, and progressively optimized using <mark>iterate_plan</mark>:

```python
{
    "title": "bootstrap_plan.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class TravelAgent:
    def __init__(self, destinations):
        self.destinations = destinations

    def bootstrap_plan(self, preferences, budget): # [!code highlight]
        plan, total_cost = [], 0
        for dest in self.destinations:
            if (total_cost + dest['cost'] <= budget
                    and self.match_preferences(dest, preferences)):
                plan.append(dest)
                total_cost += dest['cost']
        return plan

    def match_preferences(self, destination, preferences):
        return all(destination.get(k) == v for k, v in preferences.items())

    def iterate_plan(self, plan, preferences, budget): # [!code highlight]
        for i in range(len(plan)):
            for dest in self.destinations:
                if (dest not in plan
                        and self.match_preferences(dest, preferences)
                        and self.calculate_cost(plan, dest) <= budget):
                    plan[i] = dest
                    break
        return plan

    def calculate_cost(self, plan, new_dest):
        return sum(d['cost'] for d in plan) + new_dest['cost']

destinations = [
    {"name": "Paris",    "cost": 1000, "activity": "sightseeing"},
    {"name": "Tokyo",    "cost": 1200, "activity": "shopping"},
    {"name": "New York", "cost": 900,  "activity": "sightseeing"},
    {"name": "Sydney",   "cost": 1100, "activity": "beach"},
]

agent = TravelAgent(destinations)
initial_plan = agent.bootstrap_plan({"activity": "sightseeing"}, budget=2000)
refined_plan  = agent.iterate_plan(initial_plan, {"activity": "sightseeing"}, budget=2000)
print("Initial:", initial_plan)
print("Refined:", refined_plan)
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Goal Bootstrapping Loop"
}
---
flowchart TD
    Goal["Define Clear Goal\n(e.g., maximize satisfaction, budget ≤ $2000)"]
    --> Bootstrap["bootstrap_plan\nCreate initial plan based on goal & budget"]
    --> Execute["Execute Plan"]
    --> Eval{Evaluate Results}
    Eval -->|"Can be improved"| Iterate["iterate_plan\nReplace with better destinations"]
    Iterate --> Execute
    Eval -->|"Optimal"| Done["Finalize Travel Plan"]
```

---

### Taking advantage of LLM for Re-ranking and Scoring

<mark>LLM Re-ranking</mark> is a technique where instead of using initial retrieval results directly, an LLM evaluates the relevance and quality of each candidate and reorders them into an optimal sequence.

| Stage | Description |
|---|---|
| **Retrieval** | Initial retrieval of candidate documents/responses based on the query |
| **Re-ranking** | LLM reorders candidates by relevance and quality — placing the most helpful information at the top |
| **Scoring** | LLM assigns scores to each candidate to select the optimal response or document |

Example of an LLM re-ranking and scoring destinations based on user preferences in a travel agent:

```python
{
    "title": "llm_reranking.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
import requests

class TravelAgent:
    def __init__(self, destinations):
        self.destinations = destinations

    def get_recommendations(self, preferences, api_key, endpoint): # [!code highlight]
        prompt = self.generate_prompt(preferences)
        headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
        }
        payload = {"prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 150, "temperature": 0.7}

        response = requests.post(endpoint, headers=headers, json=payload)
        recommendations = response.json()["choices"][0]["text"].strip().split("\n")
        return recommendations

    def generate_prompt(self, preferences): # [!code word:generate_prompt]
        prompt = "Rank and score these destinations based on user preferences:\n"
        for key, value in preferences.items():
            prompt += f"{key}: {value}\n"
        prompt += "\nDestinations:\n"
        for dest in self.destinations:
            prompt += f"- {dest['name']}: {dest['description']}\n" # [!code highlight]
        return prompt

destinations = [
    {"name": "Paris",    "description": "City of lights, art, fashion, and culture."},
    {"name": "Tokyo",    "description": "Ultramodern city, famous for modernity and temples."},
    {"name": "New York", "description": "Iconic landmarks and diverse culture."},
    {"name": "Sydney",   "description": "Beautiful harbour city, opera house and beaches."},
]

preferences = {"activity": "sightseeing", "culture": "diverse"}
agent = TravelAgent(destinations)
recommendations = agent.get_recommendations(preferences, api_key, endpoint)
for rec in recommendations:
    print(rec)
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "LLM Re-ranking & Scoring Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    Query["User Preferences\nactivity: sightseeing\nculture: diverse"]
    --> Retrieve["Initial Candidate List\n(Paris, Tokyo, NYC, Sydney)"]
    --> Prompt["generate_prompt()\nInclude preferences + destination descriptions"]
    --> LLM["LLM (Azure OpenAI)\nEvaluate relevance & quality"]
    LLM --> Rerank["Re-ranking\nSort best-matching destinations to the top"]
    Rerank --> Score["Scoring\nAssign scores to each candidate"]
    Score --> Result["Final Recommendations\n(Including ranks & scores)"]
```

```adcard
```

---

### RAG: Prompting Technique vs Tool

<mark>RAG</mark> can be utilized in two ways: as a prompting technique or as an integrated tool:

| Aspect | Prompting Technique | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| **Approach** | Manually crafting prompts for each query | Automating retrieval and generation |
| **Control** | Fine-grained control over the retrieval process | Full end-to-end automated handling |
| **Flexibility** | Custom prompts tailored to specific requirements | More efficient for large-scale implementations |
| **Complexity** | Requires writing and tuning prompts | Easy to integrate into AI Agent architectures |

```python
{
    "title": "rag_prompting_vs_tool.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
# Prompting Technique: Manual query construction # [!code highlight]
def search_museums_in_paris():
    prompt = "Find top museums in Paris"
    return search_web(prompt)

# Tool: Automated handling via RAG system # [!code highlight]
class Travel_Agent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rag_tool = RAGTool() # [!code word:RAGTool]

    def get_museums_in_paris(self):
        user_input = "I want to visit museums in Paris."
        return self.rag_tool.retrieve_and_generate(user_input)
```

---

### Evaluating Relevancy

<mark>Relevancy evaluation</mark> is the process of continuously verifying that the information retrieved and generated by the agent is appropriate and accurate for the user's query.

Core concepts of relevancy evaluation:

| Concept | Description |
|---|---|
| **Context Awareness** | Understanding query context to retrieve relevant information (e.g., considering user budget and preferences) |
| **Accuracy** | Provided information must be factually correct and up-to-date |
| **User Intent** | Inferring the purpose behind the query to provide the most relevant information |
| **Feedback Loop** | Continuously collecting and analyzing user feedback to refine the relevancy evaluation process |

Practical relevancy evaluation techniques:

```python
{
    "title": "relevancy_techniques.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
def relevance_score(item, query): # [!code word:relevance_score]
    score = 0
    if item['category'] in query['interests']: # [!code highlight]
        score += 1
    if item['price'] <= query['budget']: # [!code highlight]
        score += 1
    if item['location'] == query['destination']: # [!code highlight]
        score += 1
    return score

def filter_and_rank(items, query): # [!code word:filter_and_rank]
    ranked_items = sorted(
        items,
        key=lambda item: relevance_score(item, query),
        reverse=True, # [!code highlight]
    )
    return ranked_items[:10]  # Return top 10

def adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback, items):
    for item in items:
        if item['name'] in feedback['liked']:
            item['relevance'] += 1 # [!code highlight]
        if item['name'] in feedback['disliked']:
            item['relevance'] -= 1 # [!code highlight]
    return items
```

Complete example applying relevancy evaluation to a Travel Agent:

```python
{
    "title": "travel_agent_relevancy.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class Travel_Agent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.user_preferences = {}

    def gather_preferences(self, preferences):
        self.user_preferences = preferences

    def generate_recommendations(self):
        flights, hotels, attractions = self.retrieve_information()
        ranked_hotels = self.filter_and_rank(hotels, self.user_preferences) # [!code highlight]
        return create_itinerary(flights, ranked_hotels, attractions)

    def filter_and_rank(self, items, query):
        return sorted(
            items,
            key=lambda item: self.relevance_score(item, query),
            reverse=True,
        )[:10]

    def relevance_score(self, item, query): # [!code word:relevance_score]
        score = 0
        if item['category'] in query['interests']:
            score += 1
        if item['price'] <= query['budget']:
            score += 1
        if item['location'] == query['destination']:
            score += 1
        return score

    def adjust_based_on_feedback(self, feedback, items):
        for item in items:
            if item['name'] in feedback['liked']:
                item['relevance'] += 1
            if item['name'] in feedback['disliked']:
                item['relevance'] -= 1
        return items

travel_agent = Travel_Agent()
preferences = {
    "destination": "Paris",
    "budget": "moderate",
    "interests": ["museums", "cuisine"],
}
travel_agent.gather_preferences(preferences)
itinerary = travel_agent.generate_recommendations()

feedback = {"liked": ["Louvre Museum"], "disliked": ["Eiffel Tower (too crowded)"]}
updated_items = travel_agent.adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback, itinerary['hotels'])
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Relevancy Evaluation Flow"
}
---
flowchart TD
    Pref["User Preferences\n{destination, budget, interests}"]
    --> GenRec["generate_recommendations()\nStart itinerary generation"]
    GenRec --> Retrieve["retrieve_information()\nSearch flights, hotels, attractions"]
    Retrieve --> Rank["filter_and_rank(hotels)\nSort by relevance_score → Top 10"]
    Rank --> Score["relevance_score(item, query)\nScore matching category, price, location"]
    Score --> Itin["create_itinerary()\nGenerate final itinerary"]
    Itin --> FB["User Feedback\n{liked, disliked}"]
    FB --> Adjust["adjust_based_on_feedback()\nAdjust relevance +1 / -1"]
    Adjust -->|"Reflect in next recommendation"| Rank
```

```adcard
```

### Search with Intent

<mark>Intent-aware Search</mark> goes beyond keyword matching to identify the actual intent behind a user's query, providing more relevant results.

Three intent types:

| Intent | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Informational** | Information gathering | "What are good museums to visit in Paris?" |
| **Navigational** | Navigating to a specific website or page | "Official Louvre Museum website" |
| **Transactional** | Executing transactions such as booking or purchasing | "Book flight to Paris" |

```python
{
    "title": "search_with_intent.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
def identify_intent(query): # [!code word:identify_intent]
    if "book" in query or "purchase" in query:
        return "transactional" # [!code highlight]
    elif "website" in query or "official" in query:
        return "navigational" # [!code highlight]
    else:
        return "informational" # [!code highlight]

def analyze_context(query, user_history):
    return {"current_query": query, "user_history": user_history}

def search_with_intent(query, preferences, user_history):
    intent = identify_intent(query)
    context = analyze_context(query, user_history)

    if intent == "informational":
        results = search_web(f"best {preferences['interests']} in {preferences['destination']}")
    elif intent == "navigational":
        results = search_web(query)
    elif intent == "transactional":
        results = search_web(f"book {query} to {preferences['destination']}")

    return personalize_results(results, user_history)

# Example usage
query = "best museums in Paris"
user_history = ["Louvre Museum website", "Book flight to Paris"]
results = search_with_intent(query, preferences, user_history)
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Intent-Aware Search Flow"
}
```

<mark>Code Generating Agents</mark> use AI models to write and execute code to solve complex problems.

#### Leveraging Environmental Awareness and Reasoning

<mark>Schema-based environmental awareness</mark> is an approach where the agent understands table schemas and reasons about which fields to adjust and how based on feedback.

```python
{
    "title": "schema_awareness.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
def adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback, preferences, schema): # [!code highlight]
    if "liked"    in feedback: preferences["favorites"] = feedback["liked"]
    if "disliked" in feedback: preferences["avoid"]     = feedback["disliked"]
    # Infer and adjust relevant fields based on schema # [!code highlight]
    for field in schema:
        if field in preferences:
            preferences[field] = adjust_based_on_environment(feedback, field, schema)
    return preferences

def adjust_based_on_environment(feedback, field, schema): # [!code word:adjust_based_on_environment]
    if field in feedback["liked"]:
        return schema[field]["positive_adjustment"]
    elif field in feedback["disliked"]:
        return schema[field]["negative_adjustment"]
    return schema[field]["default"]

# Define schema
schema = {
    "favorites": {"positive_adjustment": "increase", "negative_adjustment": "decrease", "default": "neutral"},
    "avoid":     {"positive_adjustment": "decrease", "negative_adjustment": "increase", "default": "neutral"},
}

preferences = {"favorites": "sightseeing", "avoid": "crowded places"}
feedback    = {"liked": ["Louvre Museum"], "disliked": ["Eiffel Tower (too crowded)"]}
updated_preferences = adjust_based_on_feedback(feedback, preferences, schema)

updated_flight_code = generate_code_to_fetch_data(updated_preferences)
updated_hotel_code  = generate_code_to_fetch_hotels(updated_preferences)
updated_flights = execute_code(updated_flight_code)
updated_hotels  = execute_code(updated_hotel_code)

updated_itinerary = generate_itinerary(updated_flights, updated_hotels, feedback["liked"])
print("Updated Itinerary:", updated_itinerary)
```

#### Using SQL as a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Technique

<mark>SQL as RAG</mark> generates dynamic SQL queries based on user input to retrieve information from a database:

```python
{
    "title": "sql_as_rag.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
import sqlite3

def generate_sql_query(table, preferences): # [!code word:generate_sql_query]
    conditions = [f"{k}='{v}'" for k, v in preferences.items()]
    return f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions)

def execute_sql_query(query, database="travel.db"): # [!code word:execute_sql_query]
    connection = sqlite3.connect(database)
    cursor = connection.cursor()
    cursor.execute(query)
    results = cursor.fetchall()
    connection.close()
    return results

def generate_recommendations(preferences): # [!code highlight]
    flights     = execute_sql_query(generate_sql_query("flights",     preferences))
    hotels      = execute_sql_query(generate_sql_query("hotels",      preferences))
    attractions = execute_sql_query(generate_sql_query("attractions", preferences))
    return {"flights": flights, "hotels": hotels, "attractions": attractions}

travel_agent = Travel_Agent()
preferences = {
    "destination": "Paris",
    "dates": "2025-04-01 to 2025-04-10",
    "budget": "moderate",
    "interests": ["museums", "cuisine"],
}
travel_agent.gather_preferences(preferences)
itinerary = generate_recommendations(preferences)
print("Suggested Itinerary:", itinerary)
```

### Example of Metacognition

Here is a <mark>metacognition implementation example</mark> that integrates the concepts learned so far.  
It implements a 3-step cycle where the agent **makes an initial decision → recognizes errors through self-reflection → adjusts its strategy**:

```python
{
    "title": "hotel_metacognition.py",
    "ln": true
}
---
class HotelRecommendationAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.previous_choices = []
        self.corrected_choices = []
        self.recommendation_strategies = ['cheapest', 'highest_quality'] # [!code highlight]

    def recommend_hotel(self, hotels, strategy): # [!code word:recommend_hotel]
        if strategy == 'cheapest':
            recommended = min(hotels, key=lambda x: x['price'])
        elif strategy == 'highest_quality':
            recommended = max(hotels, key=lambda x: x['quality'])
        self.previous_choices.append((strategy, recommended))
        return recommended

    def reflect_on_choice(self): # [!code highlight]
        if not self.previous_choices:
            return "No choices made yet."

        last_strategy, last_choice = self.previous_choices[-1]
        feedback = self.get_user_feedback(last_choice)

        if feedback == "bad":
            # Switch strategy: cheapest ↔ highest_quality # [!code highlight]
            new_strategy = 'highest_quality' if last_strategy == 'cheapest' else 'cheapest'
            self.corrected_choices.append((new_strategy, last_choice))
            return f"Reflecting: adjusting strategy to '{new_strategy}'."
        return "The choice was good. No need to adjust."

    def get_user_feedback(self, hotel):
        if hotel['price'] < 100 or hotel['quality'] < 7:
            return "bad"
        return "good"

hotels = [
    {'name': 'Budget Inn',     'price': 80,  'quality': 6},
    {'name': 'Comfort Suites', 'price': 120, 'quality': 8},
    {'name': 'Luxury Stay',    'price': 200, 'quality': 9},
]

agent = HotelRecommendationAgent()

# Step 1: Recommend using 'cheapest' strategy
recommended = agent.recommend_hotel(hotels, 'cheapest')
print(f"Recommended: {recommended['name']}")  # Budget Inn

# Step 2: Self-reflection → Adjust strategy (quality 6 < 7 → "bad")
print(agent.reflect_on_choice())  # adjusting to 'highest_quality'

# Step 3: Re-recommend with adjusted strategy
adjusted = agent.recommend_hotel(hotels, 'highest_quality')
print(f"Adjusted: {adjusted['name']}")  # Luxury Stay
```

```mermaid
{
    "title": "Metacognition: Reflect & Adjust Loop"
}
---
flowchart TD
    Start["Initial Decision\nrecommend_hotel('cheapest')"]
    --> Eval["Self-Reflection\nreflect_on_choice()"]
    Eval --> Feedback{User Feedback}
    Feedback -->|"'bad'\nprice < 100 or quality < 7"| Switch["Switch Strategy\n'cheapest' → 'highest_quality'"]
    Switch --> Retry["Re-recommend\nrecommend_hotel('highest_quality')"]
    Retry --> Eval
    Feedback -->|"'good'"| Done["Confirm Recommendation"]
```

This is the essence of <mark>metacognition</mark>:
- **Initial Decision**: Selected Budget Inn with the 'cheapest' strategy
- **Self-Reflection**: Recognized "bad" feedback due to quality 6
- **Strategy Adjustment**: Ultimately recommended Luxury Stay

The agent does not simply alter the final recommendation; it **modifies its own decision-making mechanism**.

- <mark>Metacognition</mark> is the ability of an agent to recognize and modify its own decision-making process, representing an **improvement of the reasoning strategy itself** rather than a simple correction of outputs.
- <mark>Corrective RAG</mark> implements an iterative self-correction loop that incorporates user feedback into preferences/avoids, rewrites queries, and performs re-retrieval.
- <mark>Pre-emptive Context Load</mark> pre-loads known domain knowledge into memory to provide instant responses without external retrieval, making it highly effective when latency is critical.
- <mark>Intent-aware Search</mark> classifies queries into Informational, Navigational, or Transactional intents, delivering far more relevant results than simple keyword matching.
- <mark>Code Generation + SQL as RAG</mark> empowers agents to dynamically write and execute code to retrieve real-time data and automate complex tasks.
